comparator.name: Political Science: International Relations and Organisations (IRO)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product and programme-specific regulations establish a coherent 180-EC International Relations and Organisations route. Year one is 60 EC in international organisations and relations, political science, actors in world politics, economics, global history, comparative politics, EU politics, research methods and statistics. Year two is 60 EC: eleven fixed 5-EC courses plus one of Contemporary Political Philosophy or Rational Choice Theory; the first-listed Contemporary Political Philosophy is selected by neutral official order. Year three is one 10-EC bachelor seminar, a 20-EC bachelor project and 30 EC genuine open elective space. Political Leadership in International Relations is the first-listed current 10-EC seminar and is selected by neutral official order. Zero-credit academic-career, career-preparation and information items are omitted.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names International Relations and Organisations (IRO), which Leiden confirms as a current formal direction in the Political Science bachelor. The exact IRO route is reconstructed; the separate National and International Politics direction is not combined with it.

alternatives.label: International Relations, Organisations and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR's full political-science sequence with international and EU law, economics, history, quantitative and qualitative methods, and communication. The label reflects the programme's balanced IRO core rather than presenting any one supporting discipline as the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Leiden's IRO route: a broad programme in international-relations theory, international organisations and law, comparative politics, EU governance, conflict and security, international political economy, global history, and quantitative and qualitative research. UCR assembles this through several disciplines rather than reproducing Leiden's integrated Political Science major and dedicated bachelor project.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON312, BENECON311); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses (Law Society & Justice, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Economics) are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Comparative Constitutional Law's prerequisite chain, European Union Politics, Persuasive Communication, Econometrics, Peace & Conflict, Foundations of European Union Law) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so foundational training precedes advanced work. Where an advisory continuation exists in the course evidence, it is honoured: Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Econometrics (semester 6); The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Persuasive Communication (semester 5); and Theory of International Relations (semester 2) precedes the more advanced European Union Politics (semester 5) and Peace & Conflict (semester 6). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: International Security, Law and Global Governance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum deliberately shifts five courses from general economics, sociology and communication into criminal and EU law, security history, political extremism, data science and a research seminar. Its title accurately states that narrower organising concentration.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route concentrating on threats to international order and the institutions used to govern them: peace and conflict, organised crime and radicalisation, public international and EU law, human rights, comparative constitutional systems, security history, and quantitative, qualitative and data-science methods. It preserves IRO foundations while giving less space to the closest route's broad political-economy and communication coverage.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312, GOSLAWJ211) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON312); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (Foundations of European Union Law, European Union Politics, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Econometrics, Peace & Conflict, History Research Seminar) is concentrated in semesters 4-6. Where an advisory continuation exists, it is honoured: Law Society & Justice (semester 1) precedes the more advanced Introduction to Public International Law (semester 2), Criminal Law & Criminal Justice (semester 3), Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law (semester 4); Introduction to Data Science (semester 4) precedes the more advanced Machine Learning (semester 5); and Theory of International Relations (semester 2) precedes the more advanced European Union Politics (semester 5) and Peace & Conflict (semester 6). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: This security, law and governance concentration replaces Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication and Introduction to Sociology with Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, History Research Seminar, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning and Youth Resilience to Extremism. The two programmes therefore differ by five courses (37.5 EC) each way, above the four-course/30-EC floor, and the changes follow directly from the narrower security, law and data-governance concept rather than arbitrary substitution.

selection.assessment: All programme-interest rows linked to this split target are marked inherited-across-split-targets and are therefore used only as discovery context, not as construction evidence. The exact IRO concepts are independently established from Leiden's current route page, study product and regulations. The closest match covers the route's required international relations, organisations, comparative politics, EU, political economy, security, law and research-methods structure. A second route, supported directly by the official IRO curriculum, concentrates on international security, law and data-informed global governance; it passes coherence, feasibility and five-course distinctness and is included. A third political-economy/EU-governance route was tested but rejected because the closest match already schedules UCR's full relevant economics cluster together with EU politics and EU law, leaving no substantively new 24-course curriculum.

blocks: International relations, comparative politics and political theory
Both examine political theory and normative questions; UCR introduces major traditions rather than Leiden’s contemporary advanced course.
Both establish comparative-politics concepts and methods for analysing political systems.
Both analyse international-relations theories and their use in explaining state behaviour.
The selected Leiden bachelor seminar is a dedicated advanced study of political leadership in international relations; no scheduled UCR course reproduces that seminar.
Introduction to Political Science is a separately credited disciplinary foundation; the selected UCR politics courses divide that foundation across specialised courses and cannot be matched twice.
Both provide historical context for contemporary international politics; UCR focuses on modern global history.
International organisations, security, EU politics and law
Public international law is a central legal architecture of international organisations; UCR approaches the institutions through law.
Both directly examine international security, conflict and responses to political violence.
Both examine European Union institutions, decision-making and politics.
Both address human rights and international legal order, with UCR integrating legal and philosophical perspectives.
Both compare political and constitutional systems; UCR approaches the comparison through constitutional law.
Both establish economic principles needed for political-economy analysis.
International Macroeconomics directly supports analysis of trade, monetary relations and international political economy.
Leiden requires a dedicated International Development course; no scheduled UCR course reproduces its political-science framing.
Leiden requires Environmental Politics; the selected UCR curricula contain no dedicated environmental-politics course.
Both introduce research design, operationalisation, sampling and empirical analysis.
Econometrics develops estimators and hypothesis testing relevant to Leiden’s second statistics course.
Both train qualitative research design and methods in social and political inquiry.
Both require students to design and execute advanced research; UCR applies this in a historical research seminar.
UCR’s Research Methods & Statistics course is already matched to Leiden’s introductory research-methods unit and cannot separately reproduce Statistics I.
Leiden’s integrated qualitative-and-quantitative academic-skills unit has no separate scheduled UCR equivalent.
Both develop argumentation and communication skills used to analyse and represent actors in world politics; UCR is a rhetoric course rather than political science.
Both develop advanced evidence-based political argumentation and communication; UCR does not reproduce the introductory IR content of Leiden’s combined unit.
Leiden requires a 20-EC independent bachelor project; UCR’s standardised Optional independent research element is shown in this row rather than treating a scheduled course as a thesis.
This is genuine approved elective, minor, exchange or internship space and has no universal subject content to match.

notes.text: Leiden IRO provides a dedicated two-year Political Science and International Relations sequence followed by a 10-EC advanced seminar and 20-EC bachelor project. UCR offers closely related politics, law, economics, history, sociology, communication and research courses, but its political-science catalogue is smaller and the resulting programmes are assembled across disciplines rather than reproducing Leiden's integrated IRO major and capstone.
